title: League of Legends Patch 26.20 Notes
description: Bee woo woop - the Worlds patch is here! Plenty of pro tuning, more champs return to Classic, and HEARTSTEEL are living their lives.

entries.context: Starting with this patch, you will only be able to access replays from matches you played in. Other players will no longer be able to download your replays, and third-party apps & sites will lose access to replay downloads entirely. We are making this change, alongside some restrictions on third party access to game memory, to close some security vulnerabilities that have recently been exploited by cheat developers and other bad actors to build unauthorized tools around League game data. You can read more about the full context in our Game Memory Removed for Third Party Apps Player Support article. Rest assured that this change will not impact your ability to VOD review your own matches by downloading and watching your replays directly in the League client!

entries.name: Ambessa
entries.context: Ambessa has been too reliable in her late game output for players with high mastery in all brackets, but especially pro-play.

changes.text: Damage: 5 - 30 (+25% bonus AD) ⇒ 5 - 25 (+20% bonus AD)
changes.label: Damage

entries.name: Ashe
entries.context: Ashe is one of the premier marksmen in pro play at the moment, and we're seeing her output too much raw damage given her position as the highest utility marksman in the game.

changes.text: Attack Damage per Level: 3.5 ⇒ 3
changes.label: Attack Damage per Level

entries.name: Cassiopeia
entries.context: Our changes two patches ago to Cassiopeia have been pretty good directionally, with most players being proportionally less impacted from those adjustments than pros. We're taking another swing at her early resources because of how dominant she still is in early laning, making her work a little harder to create an advantage.

changes.text: Base Health: 630 ⇒ 610
changes.label: Base Health

changes.text: Base Mana: 480 ⇒ 450
changes.label: Base Mana

entries.name: Diana
entries.context: While Diana's assassin build shines, her bruiser builds tend to be lagging a good bit behind. We want to inject a bit more power into that playstyle.

changes.text: Shield Bonus Health Ratio: 11% ⇒ 14%
changes.label: Shield Bonus Health Ratio

entries.name: Kennen
entries.context: Stacking the odds a bit more in his favor with his signature spell (in Riftbound) and offsetting Rocketbelt changes that he'll be a bit less excited about.

entries.name: Kindred
entries.context: Kindred is currently a bit weak, so we're giving them buffs in areas that won't make them much more overwhelming in early invades. Optimistically, they'd also make a pretty unique addition to the meta.

changes.text: Monster Mod: 150% ⇒ 165%
changes.label: Monster Mod

changes.text: Slow Duration: 1s ⇒ 1.5s
changes.label: Slow Duration

changes.text: Small Monster Targeting: Enabled ⇒ Removed
changes.label: Small Monster Targeting

entries.name: K'Sante
entries.context: Warding off this warden from being as reliable as a blind pick in coordinated play - hurting early mana and consistent W damage reduction, which should be skewed for elite audiences.

changes.text: W Base/All-Out Damage Reduction: 30 / 75% ⇒ 25 / 70%
changes.label: W Base/All-Out Damage Reduction

entries.name: Lillia
entries.context: Last patch we looked to inject a bit more power into the deer, but didn't quite see the movement we were looking for. We believe there is a bit more room for her to really prance around various levels of play so we are following up with another buff that'll really help her shine.

changes.text: Duration: 2.5s ⇒ 2.5 / 2.75 / 3s
changes.label: Duration

entries.name: Lucian
entries.context: Last patch's adjustment to help normalize mid and bot performance ended up landing as a nerf for bot lane, so we're following up with a buff to make up for the lost power.

changes.text: Attack Damage: 60 + 2.5/Level ⇒ 60 + 2.9/Level
changes.label: Attack Damage

entries.name: Mordekaiser
entries.context: Windows between Mordekaiser's ultimates make it hard to keep up with the pace of much of his opposition. His bread and butter (Q) can also feel less impactful as the pace of the game increases, so we think it can do more damage later on.

changes.text: Scaling Level 10-20: (+5/lvl) ⇒ (+7/lvl)
changes.label: Scaling Level 10-20

entries.name: Neeko
entries.context: Rocketbelt's adjustment this patch will probably land as a small nerf for Neeko, so we're giving her some minor compensation

entries.name: Smolder
entries.context: Smolder has lost quite a bit of power over the last few patches, with the Cleaver ranged nerf and bot lane meta changes disfavoring him significantly. We're further encouraging crit builds to bring his bruiser and full crit builds closer in power.

entries.context: We're giving Swain mid a moderate buff this patch while also making an adjustment that should help normalize his mid and bot lane performance.

entries.name: Tahm Kench
entries.context: As one of the tank supports with the lowest health regen, and many health scaling values on his abilities, Tahm Kench lost out on the recent adjustments to the support item. We're giving him compensation for that.

entries.name: Vayne
entries.context: Vayne has settled into a fairly weak spot, and while we still aren't totally happy with her top vs bot skew, we're getting closer. We're adjusting her base stats to help in bot where she needs to weather harass, and reverting a mana cost to her Q that simply felt way too bad.

changes.label: Health per 5

entries.name: Yunara
entries.context: Yunara is the leading candidate for "handshake hyperscaler do nothing" and we want to avoid that becoming the dominant meta, especially heading into worlds.

entries.context: Are you ready for MORE new old champions?! Because we are! This time around we've got an eclectic crew who have no business forming a band together. Everyone please welcome Aatrox, Caitlyn, Irelia, Karma, and Quinn to the Fields of Justice. As a note, the Act II Battle Pass will be arriving with Patch 26.21

entries.name: Aatrox
entries.context: Aatrox was just a baby, 3 patches old, when we chose to snapshot him for League Classic. He only ever had four balance changes before his rework in 2017 and subsequent rework in 2018, and we're excited to see how he'll perform again. He's an attack-focused fighter, damaging himself to gain attack speed and revive when he would be killed

changes.text: Passive - Blood Well: Aatrox's basic abilities damage himself to fill his Blood Well, which gives him bonus attack speed. If he's killed, he empties his Blood Well to revive on the spot.
changes.label: Passive - Blood Well
changes.before: Aatrox's basic abilities damage himself to fill his Blood Well, which gives him bonus attack speed. If he's killed, he empties his Blood Well to revive on the spot.

changes.label: Q - Dark Flight
changes.before: Aatrox flies up and crashes down, damaging and knocking up enemies in the area.

entries.name: Irelia
entries.context: Welcome back the 2010-2018 version of Irelia! The original Trinity Force poster child is here to even the odds no matter how bad they look. She's been Q-max, W-max, and E-max at various points in time, so see what build order works for you! She's a fast but deceptively durable fighter who loves to be the underdog.

entries.name: Karma
entries.context: Karma came out just two patches after Caitlyn and was only live for just over two years before being reworked in early 2013. Karma is arguably League's first battlemage, rewarding her for getting in the thick of it and making her stronger the more health she's missing.

entries.name: Quinn and Valor
entries.context: Quinn and Valor have returned, having only existed in this form for just over two years, from 2013-2015. Quinn is a ranged and evasive auto-attacker, while her ultimate calls in Valor to fight as a blistering-fast melee skirmisher instead.

entries.name: Fiora
entries.context: Fiora is still the game's most dominant top laner even after her last set of nerfs, so we're back for one more round. We don't want to take down her explosive ultimate any further, so we're just going for a generic damage nerf.

entries.name: Graves
entries.context: Graves came out swinging, being both wildly popular and arguably the game's strongest champion. We've got some feel-good changes to his animations, especially his critical strike one, and some less-feel-good nerfs as he desperately needs them. We're looking to preserve his bursty shotgunning and unique aspects as a tanky ADC, so that means we simply have to reduce his sustained damage.

entries.name: Fizz
entries.context: Fizz came out right behind Graves as a super strong performer, but mostly as an AP assassin in mid lane. We want to preserve both his assassin and fighter playstyles, so we're skewing our nerfs toward his higher-AP builds. We're pulling in lighter versions of a couple of nerfs from 2013 and 2015, aimed at bringing his guaranteed burst down to size, since he has so much reliable damage already with Deathfire Grasp and 75% AP ratio Lich Bane.

entries.name: Kennen
entries.context: Kennen hasn't quite reached the same heights as his other ninja compatriots and we're confident he isn't performing as well as he should. AD Kennen needs substantially more help than his other builds, so we're skewing his buffs in ways to help those players out most of all

entries.name: Nautilus
entries.context: Unlike his other water-themed friends, Nautilus didn't come out swinging. Sometimes that anchor just weighs him down… Ultimately, he's weak in all three of his main roles (Support, Jungle, Top) and we'd like to help those latter two most of all. So we're fixing one major bug while pulling in buffs and reverting nerfs from early in his lifetime, giving him more reason to soak up experience and wade into the thick of the fight.

entries.context: Hello Mayhemers! This patch, we're giving some champions and Augments that need a little love some extra attention. For champions, we're introducing champion-specific buffs that strengthen their core play patterns while also making them more accessible and satisfying to play in Mayhem. For Augments, we're continuing to focus on usability improvements. For example, Missile Split will now split when the missile reaches its end or is recast, rather than on the first target hit. We also lowered the cooldown on Triggered Inferno to show the real Samira fantasy. Let us know how these changes feel, and thank you for playing. See you on the Bridge!

changes.text: Fixed a bug where Orianna's (R) VFX and actual hitbox become misplaced if she casts (R) before the ball reaches a fast-moving ally like Nocturne.
Fixed a bug where a Sylas-stolen Depth Charge (R) from Nautilus could fizzle after Sylas lost vision of the target.
Fixed a bug where Xin Zhao's Three Talon Strike (Q) went completely on cooldown if the first attack was dodged by spells like Shen's Shadow Dash (E) or Jax's Counterstrike (E).
Fixed a bug where Shyvana's Dragon's Descent (R) ability fails to cancel enemy teleports.
Fixed a bug where Kayle's Reckoning (Q) applies the on-hit Spellblade effect from Sheen, Lich Bane, Trinity Force, and Iceborne Gauntlet.
Fixed a bug where large melee champions could auto large enemy champions and not be in immolate radius.
Fixed a bug where Rune page tabs overflow and clip the editor when owning more than 20 pages.
Fixed a bug where Sivir's Spell Shield (E) does not block Leona's Zenith Blade (E).
Fixed a bug where the tab buttons in the champion overview window are misaligned and unusable.
Fixed a bug where multiple Classic Spells icons fail to fill their entire square area.
Fixed a bug where Malphite's Flash summoner spell is disabled after using Unstoppable Force (R).
Fixed a bug where purchasing Royal Guard Fiora skin does not grant the Royal Guard Classic Chroma.
Fixed a bug where images from the Classic Mode Homepage loaded when logging into a non-Classic Mode tab.
Fixed a bug where the sorting effect is the same for the "Release Date ↑" and "Release Date ↓" selection buttons in the Collection - Portrait tab in Classic Mode.
Fixed a bug where the Recommended Sort Option is missing in Classic Store - Runes.
Fixed a bug where the Release Date Sort Option fails to sort Runes in a certain order in Classic Store - Runes.
Fixed a bug where rapidly pressing Recall gains Guinsoo's Rageblade stacks.
Fixed a bug where the Imperial Classic Chroma is missing its name in Champion Select's chroma selection for Xin Zhao.
Fixed a bug where Runaan's Hurricane Volley (P) triggers Minions' Call for Help.
Fixed a bug where Sivir's Spell Shield does not block damage from Miss Fortune's Q.
Fixed a bug where Sona's (E) ability description incorrectly states that its effect applies only to champions.
Fixed a bug where multiple Classic Items icons fail to fill their entire square area.
